options.name: Formal 15-Day Statutory Demand Notice (Pre-Litigation)
options.summary: Send a formal legal notice via Registered Speed Post AD & Email giving 15 days to refund principal + 12% interest.
options.why_it_works: Over 75% of Indian consumer/tenancy disputes settle here when the party realizes you have exact statutory citations and court readiness.

options.name: National Consumer Helpline (NCH - 1915) / INGRAM Grievance
options.summary: Lodge an online complaint at consumerhelpline.gov.in or Toll-Free 1915. Government grievance officers summon the company's Nodal Officer.
options.why_it_works: Mandatory 30-day corporate response required under Ministry of Consumer Affairs rules.

options.name: Online Consumer Commission Petition (e-Daakhil / DCDRC)
options.summary: File a direct petition before the District Consumer Commission under Section 35 CPA 2019. Zero court fee up to ₹5 Lakh.
options.why_it_works: Consumers can argue their own case without hiring a private advocate. Forum awards refund + interest + harassment compensation.

I am in receipt of your communication regarding the deduction/refusal of my refund of INR 45,000/-.

Please be advised that your stated grounds are legally untenable:
1. Under Indian law (Transfer of Property Act Sec 108(m) / Consumer Protection Act 2019 Sec 2(46)), standard boilerplate clauses and arbitrary deductions without verified third-party contractor tax invoices are legally void as unfair terms.
2. In the absence of documented mutual inspection reports and verifiable GST invoices, any unilateral withholding constitutes unauthorized retention and unjust enrichment.

I reiterate my formal demand for the immediate release of INR 45,000/- within 7 days, failing which this matter will be escalated to the National Consumer Helpline (1915) and the competent District Consumer Commission without further notice.

Sincerely,
[Complainant Name]

pillar_4_help_them_argue.objection: We are facing a major cash crunch and waiting for our Series A funding round to close in 6 months. You have to wait until then.
pillar_4_help_them_argue.intent: Passing speculative corporate financing risks onto individual workers.
pillar_4_help_them_argue.statutory_anchor: Indian Contract Act Sec 70 & MSMED Act Sec 16
pillar_4_help_them_argue.suggested_rebuttal: Under Section 70 and Section 73 of the Indian Contract Act, operational payment for completed and approved deliverables cannot be conditioned on external speculative equity financing unless specifically written into the contract. Under commercial law, withholding earned dues attracts interest, and if registered under MSME, compound interest at 3x RBI bank rate is statutorily mandatory under Section 16 MSMED Act.
